  lever 1: frame rate, and where in the pipe it pays   (ms, announce -> server receipt)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  fps              inbound      script  flush wait       total
  --------------------------------------------------------------
  30 fps         16.250 ms   0.0035 ms   0.0029 ms    55.84 ms
  60 fps          8.125 ms   0.0044 ms   0.0037 ms    47.92 ms
  120 fps         4.062 ms   0.0047 ms   0.0031 ms    43.97 ms
  240 fps         2.032 ms   0.0040 ms   0.0030 ms    41.98 ms
  480 fps         1.016 ms   0.0042 ms   0.0031 ms    41.00 ms
  inbound = waiting for the client's replication step to hand the
  announcement up. it is the ONLY client-side cost left, and frame
  rate is the only thing that moves it.

  lever 2: does connection order matter? (pole position)   (ms, announce -> server receipt)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
                                   min     p10     med     p90     max
  LUCK alone on the signal       40.01   41.25   47.92   54.59   56.25   n=40
  a heavy listener ahead of it   40.61   41.85   48.55   55.18   56.84   n=40

  lever 3: firing the redeem more than once   (ms, announce -> server receipt)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
                                   min     p10     med     p90     max
  one fire (normal)              40.00   41.25   47.93   54.59   56.25   n=40
  five fires                     40.01   41.26   47.92   54.59   56.27   n=40
  all copies ride the same replication step, so the first one lands
  at the same instant. spamming buys nothing and costs bandwidth.

  where the milliseconds actually go, measured stage by stage   (ms, announce -> server receipt)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. announcement over the wire        28.1241 ms   58.43%
                                     server -> your client, includes waiting for the client's replication step
  2. LUCK's handler                     0.0049 ms    0.01%
                                     signal fires -> the redeem is handed to the engine
  3. waiting for the outgoing flush     0.0037 ms    0.01%
                                     the engine holds your packet until the next replication step
  4. redeem over the wire              20.0000 ms   41.55%
                                     your client -> server
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  sum of stages                        48.1327 ms   (median total 47.90 ms)

  the script is 0.01011% of it. the other 99.99% is wire and frame clock.
